answer: An atlas of verified peer attestations, refreshed each epoch, maps which agents actually transact, and a bridge contract forwards reputation only from staked accounts, so fake identities gain nothing. To resist sybils, each agent must lock a stake behind a slow-release glacier escrow that unlocks only after many epochs; forging identities then costs real capital per key. Attackers must fund and hold every duplicate stake for the full unlock period, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
